summary: Completed backend + frontend validation for company finance, closings, dashboard portfolio panel, report pagination, and Excel export using a newly registered isolated test user. API regression suite and auth hardening suite passed; UI core flows passed with one non-deterministic debt-payment modal automation step.

integration_issues.flow: Debt payment modal open from debt card
integration_issues.issue: In one E2E run, pay button click did not reach visible payment dialog before timeout; repro run showed debts list still loading with no pay buttons. Treated as timing/state instability, not a confirmed product defect.

action_items: Update /app/.emergent/crons.yml endpoint placeholder to strict literal format required by spec: {BASE_URL}/api/company/cron/monthly-close (current file uses {{BASE_URL}}).
Manually verify debt payment dialog opening after debt rows finish loading, then retest with automation wait stabilization if needed.
critical_code_review_comments: CRITICAL config mismatch: /app/.emergent/crons.yml endpoint uses '{{BASE_URL}}/api/company/cron/monthly-close' while requirement specifies literal '{BASE_URL}/api/company/cron/monthly-close'. This may break scheduler substitution depending on parser.

Company and reporting API contracts validated: idempotent request_id handling, withdrawal constraints, debt overpay protection, closings job enqueue contract, report pagination, and six-sheet XLSX structure with formula-injection escaping.
Auth hardening checks passed: bcrypt $2b$, httpOnly cookie login, CORS credentialed allowlist behavior, lockout and Retry-After, and cross-origin cookie mutation guard.

rca of the issue: Debt-payment modal timeout came from automation step racing debt-list readiness. In repro, debts page still had loading state and no payable rows yet. Mitigation: wait for debt-loading to disappear and at least one pay-debt-* button before click. Separately, cron schedule config has a deterministic root cause: placeholder syntax in crons.yml deviates from required literal format.
